missing_input_classes.name: intervals:touching-endpoints
missing_input_classes.description: Intervals that share an endpoint, e.g. [(1, 3), (3, 5)].
missing_input_classes.why_likely: start <= end merges them into (1, 5), silently choosing closed-interval semantics; booking slots are usually half-open, where (1, 3) and (3, 5) do not overlap.
missing_input_classes.hypothesis_strategy: st.integers(-50, 50).flatmap(lambda a: st.tuples(st.just((a - 2, a)), st.just((a, a + 2)))).map(list)

missing_input_classes.name: intervals:unsorted
missing_input_classes.description: Intervals out of start order, e.g. [(5, 7), (1, 6)].
missing_input_classes.why_likely: The function trusts sorted input: [(5, 7), (1, 6)] merges to [(5, 7)] and loses the time from 1 to 5.
missing_input_classes.hypothesis_strategy: st.lists(st.tuples(st.integers(), st.integers()), min_size=2, unique=True).map(lambda xs: sorted(xs)[::-1])

missing_input_classes.name: intervals:inverted-pair
missing_input_classes.description: A pair whose start exceeds its end, e.g. [(5, 2)].
missing_input_classes.why_likely: Inverted pairs pass through unchanged and can mask overlaps that follow them.
missing_input_classes.hypothesis_strategy: st.lists(st.tuples(st.integers(), st.integers()).filter(lambda p: p[0] > p[1]), min_size=1)

from ledger.intervals.merge import merge_intervals


def test_touching_intervals_semantics():
    # Decide and pin down whether (1, 3) and (3, 5) touch (closed) or not (half-open).
    assert merge_intervals([(1, 3), (3, 5)]) == [(1, 5)]
